sub: - CI stage selectors: the `run` command takes mutually-exclusive `--unit` / `--integration` / `--e2e` flags so the Section 9 pipeline can split it into parallel stages — plus, since 2026-09-06, the operator-gated `--live`, which is NOT a CI stage and is reachable from no default path (a sibling `case` branch on `run`, so the 5-command discipline holds and both shells ship it at identical semantics). `--live` takes an optional third-token SELECTOR (2026-09-22) and composes one of two shapes. **Bare `--live`** is the live-Pulse suite: a leading non-priming `conductor preconditions` probe (an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 with `[PRECONDITION]` lines and no leg fires) → the ordered leg set the shells' own `live_leg_order` owns — at 2026-09-07 that is leg H (`halo-hue-encoding`, budget `live_leg_budget_sec 180`, first because its sustained stream must not sit inside leg A's silence window) → leg B1 → leg B2 → a 150 s quiet window → leg A → the driven a11y arm (read the order from `live_leg_order` in `scripts/agent-run.{sh,ps1}`, never from a count restated here) (`ensure_frontend` + the release build with `--features tauri/custom-protocol` → `npm run a11y:driven`), freezing each leg's `logs/agent-latest.jsonl` to `runs/live-suite/{leg}.jsonl` because that sink truncates per invocation. **`--live real-model`** runs the ONE real-model leg instead of the suite: `conductor preconditions --for real-model-interpretation` (the scenario's real-model posture requires the L4 handle absent or falsy under the union truthiness rule; an unmet subject refuses at exit 1 and no leg fires) → a pre-build of the capture binary → the non-recursive removal of `runs/live-suite/{rm.jsonl,rm-capture.txt,rm-capture.err}` → the grading rule's `rule_record` into `rm-capture.txt` BEFORE the leg (a non-zero exit stops the arm, so no counted drive of the series is spent) → `live_leg rm real-model-interpretation` → the `real_model_live` capture (stdout appended, stderr to `rm-capture.err`, `RUST_LOG` removed for both test invocations) → printed reminders. An unknown selector prints `usage: <script> run --live [real-model]` and exits 2 before any probe, in both shells; `boot` keeps the flagless probe. It adds no port, env var or `CONDUCTOR_*` handle, and leaves the envelope, the `status` disk read and the JSONL shapes untouched — so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree (`--unit` ⇒ the `cargo nextest run --workspace --profile ci` leg only — `cargo test --workspace --doc` and `cargo clippy` are their own separate Section 9 stages (Doctest / Lint), NOT folded into `--unit`; `--integration` ⇒ the hand-rolled MCP stub + `tauri::test` mock-runtime + in-memory/`TempDir` `runs.db` leg; `--e2e` ⇒ ensure-frontend, then a release build with `--features tauri/custom-protocol` (a plain `--release` binary loads `devUrl` and measures nothing — the feature, not the profile, decides bundle embedding), then the tauri-driver `wdio run` leg — the ROUTINE suite only (wdio default `specs` narrowed to `accessibility.e2e.ts` on 2026-09-01; the `driven` suite sits outside the 5-command harness as the operator leg described in §6/§9. **Since 2026-09-07 both shells ASSERT THE PRINTED VERDICT, not the exit code** — the leg's exit cannot separate a full pass from a total skip, because the handle guard is designed to skip at exit 0 — **and that contract holds only where the INVOKING environment does not preempt the capture-then-print: a PowerShell caller setting `$PSNativeCommandUseErrorActionPreference = $true` turns wdio's non-zero into a terminating error at the `npm run a11y` call, before the script prints the captured output or reaches its assertion, so the caller sees one `NativeCommandExitException` line and none of the verdict (as measured at `2026-09-07-sr-findings-fixed`, with a local control both ways; the CI a11y gate step's setting was removed there, both shells byte-unchanged)** — capturing wdio's output to `$RUNS_DIR/a11y-e2e.log`, reading the exit from the BARE command (never through a pipe), then requiring: zero on the `Spec Files:` failed count (a term the line OMITS when nothing failed), a per-spec skip tally within the expected-skip SET (the two live-hold subjects; a third skip is a failure, which is how a fixture-seeding failure surfaces), and the `[webview2 … windows]` driven-session banner. The leg also emits one violation record per run at `runs/a11y/<run_id>.jsonl` — a SEPARATE artifact whose shape is this §3 envelope's eleven fields PLUS the obs §9 resource tags, deliberately outside the harness's non-recursive `"$RUNS_DIR"/*.jsonl` glob so `status` cannot read it as a scenario run. The command count stays five, no stage selector was added, and the `status` disk read and per-run envelope/JSONL shapes are untouched — so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree), with the tauri-driver child spawned at `cwd` = the workspace root so the app's `resolve_under` can reach `scenarios/` (it rejects absolute paths and `..`, so the launch cwd is the only lever), and the mocha ceiling raised 60s → 15min because wdio enforces `mochaOpts.timeout` itself — headless under `xvfb` on Linux CI, headful on the Windows host). **The leg SEEDS its own subject before the session** (2026-09-02): `wdio.conf.ts`'s `seedFixtureRuns()` clean-re-creates the gitignored `runs/e2e-fixture/` and invokes `cargo test -q -p conductor-run --test envelope_fixture` with `CONDUCTOR_E2E_SEED_DIR` naming that repo-relative dir, so the subject — the committed lamps journal's records PLUS an over-envelope `run_envelope` row — is written through the production writer (`conductor_run::persist`) rather than copied; a non-zero exit or a missing journal THROWS rather than seeding silently. The tauri-driver spawn then carries `CONDUCTOR_RUNS_DIR=runs/e2e-fixture` (repo-relative — `resolve_under` rejects absolute handles), because `/runs/` is gitignored and an unseeded clean tree gives the coverage rows no run record to render; without it the populated-lamp assertions would have no subject on CI and would read host-local run residue on a dev box. The 5-command surface, the `status` disk read and the envelope/JSONL shapes are unchanged, so §3 ↔ obs-plan §3 still agree. With no flag, `run` executes the full aggregate (nextest + doctest + clippy + scenarios); per-stage target mapping is the Section 9 pipeline table.
